insight_to_chart_map.insight_summary: Paid_search users (especially Google non-brand) churn voluntarily because the generic onboarding flow doesn't match their search intent.
insight_to_chart_map.chart_reasoning: Comparing voluntary churn rate across paid_search sub-channels is a categorical comparison, sorted bar with horizontal orientation keeps sub-channel labels readable. The audience is the product team — a bar with absolute % labels beats a stacked bar because the metric is a single rate, not a composition.

alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: Adds a composition dimension that distracts from the single-rate comparison.
5 sub-channels would violate the ≤4-slice rule and obscure ranking.

insight_to_chart_map.insight_summary: The 2025-07-15 pricing change drove a Starter-tier-specific churn spike (+68% residual).
insight_to_chart_map.chart_type: Line chart with annotated change-point and tier facets
insight_to_chart_map.chart_reasoning: Time-series with a discontinuity is the textbook line-chart case. Faceting by plan_tier makes the Starter-vs-Pro contrast visually decisive. Annotation at 2025-07-15 anchors the reader to the inflection.

alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: Visually compresses the per-tier residual which is the key signal.
Loses the time dimension — the whole point is the level shift on a date.

insight_to_chart_map.insight_summary: First-feature activation is the highest-leverage product fix.
insight_to_chart_map.chart_type: Funnel chart (retained vs voluntary-churn cohorts side by side)
insight_to_chart_map.chart_reasoning: Sequential conversion is the canonical funnel-chart case. Side-by-side cohort funnels show exactly which step breaks for churners; the 46pp gap at first_feature_used reads instantly.

alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: Doesn't communicate the sequential dependence between steps.
Overkill — there are only 4 nodes and 3 transitions; a funnel is clearer for this audience.

sections.purpose: Show the pre/post discontinuity and confirm tier-specificity.
components: Line chart with 2025-07-15 marker, faceted by plan_tier

sections.purpose: Pinpoint the onboarding step that breaks for churners.

dashboard_architecture.interactivity_spec: Plan_tier and acquisition_channel filters are global. Hovering any KPI scorecard shows the 90-day sparkline. Funnel cohorts can be toggled (retained / voluntary / involuntary).

visualisation_specs.chart_name: Paid_search voluntary churn doubles in Google non-brand
visualisation_specs.purpose: Rank paid_search sub-channels by voluntary churn rate and surface the worst offender.
annotations: Google non-brand drives 47% of paid_search voluntary churn volume.
visualisation_specs.alt_text: Horizontal bar chart showing voluntary churn rate by paid_search sub-channel: Google non-brand 41 percent, Bing 35 percent, Facebook 28 percent, Google brand 18 percent. Organic baseline reference line at 14 percent.

visualisation_specs.chart_name: Pricing change drives Starter-tier-only churn spike
visualisation_specs.purpose: Show the pre/post 2025-07-15 discontinuity and confirm it's concentrated in Starter tier.
visualisation_specs.chart_type: Line chart with annotated change-point and tier facets
annotations: Starter-tier residual: +68% post-shift. Pro/Enterprise within noise.
visualisation_specs.alt_text: Three-line chart of weekly voluntary churn count by plan tier from 2025-06-03 to 2025-08-26. Starter line jumps from about 320 to about 540 per week after the 2025-07-15 marker; Pro and Enterprise lines are flat.

visualisation_specs.chart_name: Voluntary churners never reach the first feature
visualisation_specs.purpose: Pinpoint the activation step where churners and retained users diverge.
visualisation_specs.alt_text: Two side-by-side funnels for retained and voluntary-churn cohorts across signup, first login, first feature used, and weekly recurring event. The retained cohort holds at 84 percent through first feature used while the voluntary-churn cohort drops to 38 percent at the same step.

visualisation_specs.purpose: Show the underlying distribution that drove H2's odds ratio.
visualisation_specs.chart_type: Grouped box plot (log-y), faceted by acquisition_channel
visualisation_specs.alt_text: Grouped box plot of first-30-day event count on a log y-axis, by churn type, faceted by acquisition channel. Voluntary-churn boxes sit consistently below retained boxes; paid_search shows the widest gap.

anti_pattern_audit.chart_name: Pricing change drives Starter-tier-only churn spike
anti_pattern_audit.anti_pattern_found: Original draft had a truncated y-axis starting at 250 which exaggerated the post-shift jump.
anti_pattern_audit.correction_applied: Reset y-axis to start at 0; the post-shift spike still reads clearly without inflating the relative change.

anti_pattern_audit.chart_name: Voluntary churners never reach the first feature
anti_pattern_audit.anti_pattern_found: Original draft titled the chart 'Activation Funnel by Cohort' — a category label, not an insight.
anti_pattern_audit.correction_applied: Renamed to 'Voluntary churners never reach the first feature' so the title states the finding.

accessibility_review.notes: All charts use the Okabe-Ito palette. Reference-line labels are 14pt+; axis labels 12pt+; titles 18pt. Contrast checked at 4.7:1 for body text on the dashboard background.

narrative_flow.hook: Paid_search voluntary churn is more than double organic — and it's concentrated in one sub-channel.
context_sequence: The 2025-07-15 pricing change drove a Starter-tier-only spike, not a base-wide one.
Across the base, voluntary churners share one behaviour: they never reach the first feature.
narrative_flow.payoff: An intent-segmented onboarding test for paid_search Google non-brand is the highest-leverage Q4 intervention; pricing-perception mitigation should be scoped narrowly to entry-tier first-bill experience.
